title: Straight Intellects And Sound Hearts 12th 13th Degrees The Agreement Of Sound Hearts In Unveiling And Witnessing

questions.question: What did the traveler begin to study in this part?
questions.answer: He began to study upright minds and bright hearts.

questions.question: Did all the bright minds have the exact same way of thinking?
questions.answer: No. Their ways and abilities were different.

questions.question: Even though their ways were different, what was the same in them?
questions.answer: Their belief in Allah’s oneness was the same.

questions.question: How strong was their certainty?
questions.answer: It was steady and strong.

questions.question: What does their shared certainty show they were holding on to?
questions.answer: One real and unchanging truth.

questions.question: What picture is used for their agreement in faith?
questions.answer: A strong, shining chain.

questions.question: What did that shining chain open like?
questions.answer: A bright window to the truth.

questions.question: What did the traveler also notice about the witness of the bright minds?
questions.answer: Their witness matched and agreed with each other.

questions.question: What were the bright hearts turned toward?
questions.answer: They were turned toward the truth.

questions.question: What did each bright heart show like a small seat of knowledge?
questions.answer: Knowledge of the Lord.

questions.question: What were the hearts compared to because they showed the truth?
questions.answer: Windows open to the sun.

questions.question: When all those hearts are taken together, what are they like?
questions.answer: A huge mirror, like an ocean reflecting the sun.

questions.question: Why does their agreement make a trustworthy guide?
questions.answer: Because so many clear hearts and minds would not all be tricked by something false.

questions.question: What kind of people would not even accept the idea that all of them were fooled at once?
questions.answer: Even very foolish deniers would not accept that.

questions.question: After understanding all this, what did the traveler say with his mind and heart?
questions.answer: He said that he believed in Allah.

questions.question: Who are the two groups the traveler learns from in this passage?
questions.answer: Upright intellects and luminous hearts.

questions.question: Were the abilities of those intellects all alike?
questions.answer: No. Their abilities were different.

questions.question: Were their approaches and views all alike?
questions.answer: No. Some were even unlike each other.

questions.question: In spite of those differences, what belief did they all share?
questions.answer: Belief that Allah is one.

questions.question: What was alike in their confidence and certainty?
questions.answer: It was firm and sure in all of them.

questions.question: If many people with different paths agree on one faith truth, what does that suggest?
questions.answer: It suggests that the truth is real and solid.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the roots of that truth?
questions.answer: They were deep and could not be pulled out.

questions.question: What image shows that their agreement is strong and beautiful?
questions.answer: A glowing chain that cannot be broken.

questions.question: What did the traveler see about the unveilings and witnessings of sound minds?
questions.answer: They all fit together and agreed.

questions.question: How are the luminous hearts described in relation to truth?
questions.answer: They were connected to it and showed it.

questions.question: What does each heart act like?
questions.answer: A little throne of knowledge and a wide mirror.

questions.question: What does “like windows to the sun” help us understand about the hearts?
questions.answer: They let truth be seen clearly.

questions.question: What are all the hearts together compared to?
questions.answer: A great mirror, like a sea reflecting sunlight.

questions.question: Why can falsehood not explain this united witness?
questions.answer: Because one false idea cannot fool many sharp minds and hearts in the same clear way.

questions.question: What was the traveler’s response after seeing this unity?
questions.answer: He affirmed his faith in Allah.

questions.question: At the start of the passage, what did the traveler notice about enlightened minds?
questions.answer: He noticed that they shared the same belief about Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: Did those minds all have one level of ability?
questions.answer: No. They had different levels.

questions.question: Did they all follow one method?
questions.answer: No. Their methods were different.

questions.question: What stayed the same even when their methods differed?
questions.answer: Their strong belief and certainty.

questions.question: What does one shared certainty among many minds point to?
questions.answer: It points to one true source.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the roots of their belief?
questions.answer: As deep and impossible to pull out.

questions.question: What does the traveler call their shared faith in Allah’s existence and oneness?
questions.answer: A bright chain that cannot be broken.

questions.question: What kind of opening did that chain become?
questions.answer: An opening toward the world of truth.

questions.question: What did the traveler see about the experiences of the sound, bright minds?
questions.answer: Their experiences agreed with one another.

questions.question: What were the luminous hearts doing with the truth?
questions.answer: They were facing it, joined to it, and showing it.

questions.question: What two things is each heart compared to?
questions.answer: A small throne and a broad mirror.

questions.question: What is the “Sun of the Truth” helping us picture?
questions.answer: The truth as clear, bright, and life-giving.

questions.question: What are the many hearts like when seen all together?
questions.answer: Like one great mirror or a sea reflecting the sun.

questions.question: Why is their agreement called a perfect guide and teacher?
questions.answer: Because it is dependable and leads to what is true.

questions.question: What final words show the traveler accepted this lesson?
questions.answer: He said he believed in Allah.

questions.question: What did all the luminous intellects agree about?
questions.answer: They agreed about Allah’s necessary existence and His oneness.

questions.question: Were their opinions alike because they were all the same kind of people?
questions.answer: No. They had different abilities, ways, and views.

questions.question: Why is their agreement important even though they are different?
questions.answer: Because it shows they are meeting on one real truth.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the truth they depend on?
questions.answer: It does not change.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the strength of that truth in them?
questions.answer: It is deep-rooted and cannot be uprooted.

questions.question: What symbol is used for their united faith?
questions.answer: A shining chain.

questions.question: What can be seen through that chain, in a picture word?
questions.answer: A bright opening to truth.

questions.question: What else agreed besides their beliefs?
questions.answer: Their unveilings and witnessings also agreed.

questions.question: What kind of hearts are mentioned with those agreeing witnessings?
questions.answer: Healthy, bright hearts.

questions.question: Why are the hearts compared to windows?
questions.answer: Because they let the light of truth be seen.

questions.question: Why are all the hearts together compared to an ocean reflecting sunlight?
questions.answer: Because many hearts together show truth in a great and beautiful way.

questions.question: According to the passage, could a wrong idea fool all these clear minds at once?
questions.answer: No. That is not believable.

questions.question: What does the passage say about even very foolish deniers?
questions.answer: They still would not agree with such a bad claim.

questions.question: How did the traveler answer this lesson with both mind and heart?
questions.answer: He declared his faith in Allah.

questions.question: Who had a united belief in this passage?
questions.answer: The luminous intellects did.

questions.question: What was united in them?
questions.answer: Their belief in Allah’s unity.

questions.question: What does the passage say about their outlooks?
questions.answer: They were different, and some even opposed others.

questions.question: What does it mean when people with different views still agree on one truth?
questions.answer: It means the truth is very strong and clear.

questions.question: What kind of certainty did they have?
questions.answer: Strong and settled certainty.

questions.question: What was impossible to pull out from them?
questions.answer: Their deep-rooted truth.

questions.question: How is their shared faith described in a way we can imagine?
questions.answer: Like a bright chain that cannot break.

questions.question: What did the traveler notice about the witness of the sound intellects?
questions.answer: It matched and fit together.

questions.question: What were the luminous hearts like in relation to truth?
questions.answer: They were connected to it and made it visible.

questions.question: What does each heart become, in the passage’s picture language?
questions.answer: A small seat of Lordly knowledge and a wide mirror.

questions.question: What do many hearts together become?
questions.answer: A very large mirror, like a shining sea.

questions.question: Why is their united witness safe to trust?
questions.answer: Because falsehood cannot keep fooling many keen minds and hearts together.

questions.question: What kind of eyes are mentioned to show careful understanding?
questions.answer: Sharp eyes.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the claim that all of them were deceived?
questions.answer: It is too corrupt and unreasonable to accept.

questions.question: After learning this, what did the traveler say?
questions.answer: He said, “I have believed in Allah.”

questions.question: What did the traveler first see about all the bright intellects?
questions.answer: He saw that they all had the same belief about Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: Did those intellects all have the same strength and style?
questions.answer: No. They differed in ability and way.

questions.question: What was one in all of them besides belief?
questions.answer: Their confidence and certainty were one.

questions.question: What does one shared certainty among many different minds point to?
questions.answer: It points to one steady truth.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the roots of that truth?
questions.answer: They were planted deep.

questions.question: What picture shows the agreement of those minds?
questions.answer: A bright, unbreakable chain.

questions.question: What did that chain open to?
questions.answer: To the world of truth.

questions.question: What did the traveler see about the witnessings of the sound intellects?
questions.answer: They agreed with each other.

questions.question: What special kind of hearts are named in the passage?
questions.answer: Sound and luminous hearts.

questions.question: What were those hearts doing with truth?
questions.answer: They were turned toward it and showing it.

questions.question: What is each heart compared to first?
questions.answer: A small throne of knowledge.

questions.question: What is each heart compared to next?
questions.answer: A broad mirror.

questions.question: What are all the hearts together compared to?
questions.answer: A great mirror, like an ocean reflecting the sun.

questions.question: Why is their agreement a high guide and teacher?
questions.answer: Because it is reliable and leads people rightly.

questions.question: What conclusion did the traveler reach in the end?
questions.answer: He came to faith in Allah with his intellect and heart.
